turns.learner: Hello again! Can we practise he, she and it with -s again today?
turns.tutor:
Of course. Let's start with recall: you clearly know the basic -s after he, she and it, so today let's sharpen the trickier spellings.
The -s ending has three forms. Plain -s covers most verbs (reads, plays). Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -s, -x or -o take -es, because the extra vowel makes the ending pronounceable (pushes, does). Consonant + y becomes -ies (carries), while vowel + y simply adds -s (enjoys).
Your task: write two sentences about a friend's weekly habits. Use one verb that needs -es and one that needs -ies, choosing verbs we have not mentioned. Then tell me in one line why "enjoy" does not change its y.
